text:
jules: filing a quick note  onboard int4-run of kestrel-lite shows funcall JSON parse spikes after tokenizer prune change. failures look like truncated UTF-8 sequences appended to otherwise-valid object.

omar: interesting, any raw bytes?

jules: uploaded raw blob to s3://canary/traces/1705002222. sample tail (utf8-hex): `7b22616374696f6e223a226c69737422307d e2 80` which is `{"action":"list0"}` + truncated “…” byte sequence. strict decoder errors.

sneha: this is different from newline/control-char tails we've seen. here the stream ends mid-multibyte char which makes parsers raise UnicodeDecodeError. appears when final token is a multibyte punctuation and model generated partial byte on final flush.

kai: canary-bot shows these are correlated with kernel flush at exactly 64-byte chunk boundary and batch_size=1. batching >1 tends to merge chunks and hide truncation.

becky: mitigation idea: in stream consumer, on decode error, attempt a UTF-8 repair step that drops trailing incomplete seqs: `payload_bytes.rstrip(b'\x80-\xBF')` until valid UTF-8. then run strict JSON parse and tag telemetry `rescue=utf8_trim`.

omar: sounds ok as temporary. long-term fix: ensure kernel always completes multibyte sequences on flush (quant team needs a small change to flush semantics). opened QNT-512.

kai: add guard: if repair removes >4 bytes or removes bytes inside object quotes, escalate to manual review; don't silently fix big corruption. also run golden correctness check on 2k samples to ensure no behavior drift.

sneha: action items: becky to prototype utf8-trim rescue + telemetry today, jules to attach sample reproducer & link to QNT-512, kai to add alert if `rescue=utf8_trim` >2% for 30m. i'll run 4h soft-canary with repair flag toggled.

canary-bot: deploy kestrel-lite-int4-canary @ 1705000000 -> hosts p,q,r. current failures 8/80 in last 20m.

jules: thanks all. let's keep rescue feature-flagged until kernel fix lands. will share canary graphs when done. :rocket:
